pressReleaseTitle: India Rating Upgrades B.G. Shirke Construction Technology’s Bank Loan Facilities to ‘IND AA-’; Outlook Stable
issuerName: B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd.
overview: India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) has upgraded B.G. Shirke Construction Technology Pvt. Ltd’s (BGSCTPL) bank loan facilities’ long-term rating to ‘IND AA-’ with a Stable Outlook from ‘IND A+’ while affirming the short-term rating at ‘IND A1+’ as follows:
overviewHTML: Ind-Ra continues to take a standalone view of  BGSCPTL to arrive at the ratings while factoring in the equity support to be provided to its subsidiaries over the medium term.
keyRatingDrivers:
Strong Operating Performance: BGSCTPL continues to demonstrate robust operating performance with FY26 revenue likely to remain broadly in line with FY25 levels at about INR60 billion. The company’s revenue grew at a CAGR of 17% over FY21-FY25, reflecting consistent execution and sustained business momentum. In 1HFY26, the company reported revenue of INR28.2 billion (1HFY25: INR27.07 billion, FY25: INR59.16 billion; FY24: INR58.9 billion; FY23: INR57.9 billion), supported by a healthy EBITDA margin of 22.5% (24%; 22.3%; 22.1%). The margin stability is driven by strong project execution facilitated by in‑house precast facilities located near major project sites, enabling cost efficiencies.

BGSCTPL’s order book remains healthy and provides strong revenue visibility. As of December 2025, the company had an order book of INR157 billion including price escalation, under-construction contracts (end‑October 2024: INR166 billion; July 2023: INR104.9 billion; May 2022: INR124.15 billion), translating into around 2.65x of FY25 revenue, indicating strong medium‑term growth visibility. Ind-Ra expects the company to sustain the existing scale of profitability while maintaining adequate order book in FY26.

Credit Metrics to Remain Robust: BGSCTPL’s credit profile continued to strengthen in 1HFY26, supported by healthy profitability, low debt levels, and reduced interest costs. The company remained net cash positive over FY24-1HFY26, reflecting its strong balance sheet position. Its gross interest coverage (operating EBITDAR/gross interest expense) also remained robust at 11.5x in 1HFY26 (FY25: 13.7x; FY24: 11.02x), demonstrating the company’s ability to comfortably service its financial obligations.

The total outside liability/EBITDA remained comfortable at 2.2x in 1HFY26 (FY25: 2.2x; FY24: 1.9x; FY23: 2.5x), supported by healthy cash generation and controlled leverage. Ind‑Ra expects the credit metrics to remain strong over the medium term, driven by the company’s steady operating performance and efficient working capital management.

Healthy Free Cash Flows; Stable Working Capital Cycle: BGSCTPL’s operating cash flows (company reported) remained healthy at INR9.3 billion in FY25, despite a moderate decline from INR12.46 billion in FY24, supported by its robust EBITDA. The gross working capital as a percentage of revenue increased to 44% in FY25 (FY24: 36%; FY23: 31%), primarily due to higher receivable days, which were largely related to the spilling over of receivables into the next financial year. However, the net working capital as a percentage of revenue remained stable at 17% in FY25 (FY24: 17%; FY23: 14%), aided by higher mobilisation advances.

While most authorities have started charging interest on mobilisation advances, the company continues to benefit in cases where the interest rate is lower than bank lending rates or where the advances remain interest‑free. Given the reduced instances of interest-free mobilisation advances and the relative interest rate advantage, BGSCTPL’s net working capital cycle has elongated from a low single-digit historically, as the company takes advantage of price discounts by timely/advance payments to vendors. Ind-Ra expects the company’s working capital requirements to remain broadly in line with FY25 levels over the medium term, given BGSCTPL’s consistent counterparty mix and project profile.

Exposure to Group Entities: BGSCTPL maintains a modest level of exposure to group entities in the form of investments, along with loans and advances. The aggregate exposure stood at INR6.4 billion as of 1HFY26 (FY25: INR7.6 billion; FY24: INR3.4 billion), reflecting an allocation of around 17% of capital provided to group entities. A substantial portion of this exposure (FY25: around 95%) is concentrated in a few group entities namely Siporex India Pvt Ltd, BGS Redevelopment and Gas India Pvt Ltd, Shirke Recreation Enterprise and Shirke Club Management LLP.  Management plans to reduce its group company exposure by INR1.5 billion-2 billion by end-FY26. Ind-Ra does not expect any material fund outflows to support any other group company operations in the near-to-medium term, which is a rating monitorable. 

Concentrated Order Book: BGSCTPL’s construction order book remains concentrated across geographies, counterparties, and individual contracts. Approximately 89% of the order book is concentrated in Maharashtra, followed by Karnataka at 9%, and the balance in Delhi and Tamil Nadu.

About 81% of the orders are from Maharashtra state government agencies, largely Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA; 47%), City and Industrial Development Corporation of Maharashtra Limited (CIDCO; 15%), Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA; 8%), Konkan Housing and Area Development Board (4%, Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority (3%), and Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corporation (2%). Furthermore, around 30% of the order book pertains to projects that are yet to be commenced. The top five contracts accounted for 43% of the order book and the top 10 contracts for 59%. Although BGSCTPL benefits from a longstanding presence in the urban and low‑cost housing construction segment, coupled with established relationships with key state authorities, the geographical and client concentration, dependence on state‑government capex cycles, and the timely execution of contracts will continue to be a critical monitorable.
ratingSensitivities:
Positive: Sustaining the current scale of profitability while maintaining or improving diversification across segments, geographies, and counterparties; and a continued improvement in the governance structure, including stronger availability of high‑quality financial and operational data while maintaining a robust credit profile will lead to a positive rating action.

Negative: Events that could, individually or collectively, lead to a negative rating action are:
- a decline in the profitability and/or an elongation of the working capital cycle;
- any material fund outflows to any group companies/ promoter payouts, leading to deterioration in liquidity;
- the net adjusted leverage exceeding 0.75x and/or the total outside liabilities/EBITDA exceeding 3.5x on a sustained basis.
companyProfile: Incorporated in 1994 (established business in 1944), BGSCTPL is the flagship company of the Pune-based Shirke Group. The company is primarily engaged in the construction of housing projects for government agencies such as MHADA, CIDCO, MMRDA and Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana.

descriptionAboutIndiaRating:
India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) is India's SEBI registered credit rating agency committed to providing India's credit markets accurate, timely, and prospective credit opinions. Built on a foundation of independent thinking, rigorous analytics, and an open and balanced approach towards credit research, Ind-Ra has grown rapidly during the past decade, gaining significant market presence in India's fixed income market.

Ind-Ra currently maintains coverage of corporate issuers, financial institutions (including banks and insurance companies), finance companies, urban local bodies, and structured finance and project finance companies.

Headquartered in Mumbai, Ind-Ra has seven branch offices located in Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Gurugram, Hyderabad, Kolkata, and Pune. Ind-Ra is recognised by the Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India.

Ind-Ra is a 100% owned subsidiary of the Fitch Group.

detailedRationaleOfRatingAction: The upgrade reflects Ind-Ra’s expectation of the sustenance of BGSCPTL’s revenue of around INR60 billion, and an EBITDA run-rate of INR12 billion-13 billion for FY26 and FY27, the maintenance of a strong credit profile with a net cash position and a healthy liquidity position with over INR10 billion of unencumbered cash. The working capital cycle is likely to remain stable and support to group entities is likely to remain modest over the medium term. The ratings also factor in the company’s strengthened governance framework, including the presence of independent directors, reflecting adequate internal controls and financial transparency.
listOfKeyRatingDrivers:
Strengths

- Credit metrics to remain robust
- Healthy free cash flows; stable working capital cycle

Weaknesses
- Exposure to group entities
- Concentrated order book
liquidity: Adequate: The company’s average utilisation of the fund-based and non-fund-based working capital limits was 27% and 65%, respectively, over the 12 months ended December 2025. The company’s fund-based and non-fund-based limits are largely from public sector banks.  BGSCTPL had unencumbered cash and cash equivalents including mutual funds of INR15.48 billion at 1HFYE26 (FYE25: INR13.77 billion; FYE24: INR 10.8 billion), against scheduled repayments of INR0.94 billion and INR0.37 billion in FY26 and FY27, respectively, which will be repaid from internal accruals. The agency believes that the low utilisation of fund-based limits and substantial cash balance provide strong balance sheet flexibility.
